audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding passages are present verbatim at the stated locators in the copies we hold (Aso 2010 IRL the text layer; Urabe 2022 chapter the text layer/168-171). (2) The classification 'tonal' (tonal-OR-pitch accent, no stress rule) rests on two open grammar sketches (2010, 2022). Yaeyama-go Hateruma hōgen no akusento taikei no saikentō: shiki to kaku ni motozuku bunseki [Reexamining the prosodic system of the Hateruma dialect of Yaeyaman: an analysis based on register and accent kernel]. Onsei Kenkyu (J. Phonetic Society of Japan) 29(3): 183-197.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Harvard-Yenching Library (offsite storage), call number P215 .O55x; Harvard-Yenching Library, call number (J) P215 .O55x
sources.quote: Summary p.183: 'In this dialect, the prosodic word functions as the counting unit. Each of the two traditionally recognized accent types Level and Rising can be further divided into two subtypes, depending on where the pitch fall occurs: after the first or second prosodic word ... a new interpretation of Hateruma's prosodic system, formulated in terms of register and accent kernel.' Conclusion p.194 recognises five types L0, L1, L2, H1, H2 (register x kernel). Purely lexical tone/accent; no stress.
sources.locator: English summary p.183; sec. 6 conclusion p.194 (the text layer)
sources.note: Latest analysis of Hateruma (prosodic word as counting unit; register x kernel, five classes); most current statement of the system our record describes.

sources.citation: Celik, Kenan & Reiko Aso. 2024. Minami Ryūkyū Yaeyama-go Kohama hōgen no sankei akusento taikei [The three pattern prosodic system of the Kohama dialect of Yaeyama Ryukyuan]. Onsei Kenkyu 28(1): 1-16.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Harvard-Yenching Library (offsite storage), call number P215 .O55x; Harvard-Yenching Library, call number (J) P215 .O55x
sources.quote: 'the Kohama dialect distinguishes between three different tone classes ... the prosodic word ... needs to be posited in order to achieve an adequate generalization of the pitch patterns of each tone class ... the three tone classes of Kohama regularly correspond to the tone classes reconstructed in proto-Ryukyuan.' A third Yaeyama dialect, same lexical-tone-class prosody, no stress.
sources.note: Extends coverage beyond the Hateruma/Shiraho sub-lineage flagged as a caveat by readers A and B: Kohama also has three lexical tone classes, no stress.

sources.quote: p.91-92: Hateruma is a 'word-tone' (語声調, Hayata 1977/1999) language; survey of 289 nouns + verbs shows 'at least present-day Hateruma has a three-pattern accent system whose domain is word + accentless particle (bunsetsu). sources.locator: Abstract p.87; sec. 4 pp.91-92 (the text layer); sec. 7 conclusion p.107 (the text layer); English abstract p.110
sources.note: Dedicated Hateruma accent study with F0 evidence that supersedes the held Aso 2010 half-page ('two distinctive pitch patterns', 'mora+2 patterns'): three-pattern N-kei word-tone system, domain = bunsetsu; our the primary-stress rule text should be updated to it.

sources.quote: Abstract: Kuroshima, 'hitherto described as a two-pattern accent system, in fact has a three-pattern accent system with three contrasting types', whose realisation requires positing the prosodic word (PWd). Fourth Yaeyama dialect, same type of system; no stress.
